newsitem.title: USA: U.S. platinum coins sell well, gold sales up too.
newsitem.headline: U.S. platinum coins sell well, gold sales up too.

text.p: The U.S. Mint's platinum coin program looks to be off to a good start, with the two proof sets issued on June 8 selling out in less than three weeks, precious metals analysts said.
"The U.S. platinum coin program could lift annual investment purchases of bullion coins to 200,000 ounces, from 100,000 ounces," CPM Group managing director Jeffrey Christian said.
The U.S. Mint issued individual proofs and proof sets on June 8.

One of the two proof sets consisted of a one-ounce, half-ounce, quarter-ounce and tenth-ounce platinum American Eagle coin, while the other included a one-ounce platinum coin, along with a one-ounce silver Eagle and a one-ounce gold Eagle coin.
The 1997 proof coins contain around 39,000 ounces of platinum.
As for the individual coin proofs, by July 10, the 5,060 one-ounce coins (63 pct of the 8,000 available) had sold by July 10, the U.S. Mint said.
The U.S. Mint is scheduled to launch the main uncirculated platinum Eagle coin program in September this year.

"The strong showing of these coins in the collectors market has stirred speculation that the bullion issues due out this fall will also meet strong demand," New York-based Platinum Guild International analyst Aran Murphy said.
Meanwhile, the premiums on the Australian Koala, the Australian Koala-Kilo, the platinum Canadian Maple Leaf, and the Isle of Man Noble were slightly lower in June.
Demand for U.S. American Eagle gold bullion coins is also running well ahead of last year, despite a dip in June.
The U.S. Mint sold 31,500 ouncess of gold coins in June, down from 47,500 ounces in May, but up sharply from June 1996.
And in the first half of 1997, sales reached 292,750 ounces, an increase of 142 percent from 121,000 ounces in the first half of 1996.
Sales of the U.S. Mint's silver Eagle also declined in June, to 220,000 ounces, from 265,000 ounces in May and 260,000 ounces in June 1996.
But sales of silver coins were significantly higher in the first six months of 1997, at 1,1741,000 ounces, up 78 percent on 978,000 ounces in the first half of 1996.
